diagnosis: Candidate/bad runs overrepeat actions without changing their approach: repeated-result operations are strongly overrepresented, especially clicks, no-ops, and scrolling.
expected_mechanism: Detecting unchanged action-state attempts and requiring a strategy change should reduce loops and wasted operations. The cost is modest bookkeeping and occasional premature switching when a retry would have succeeded.
policy_text: Track recent action-state pairs. After one unchanged retry, do not repeat the same action unless new evidence predicts success; instead inspect state, change the action or target, use a different strategy, or stop with a concise blocker report.

quantitative_evidence.command: jq -r 'select(.stack_frames[0]=="result:repeated") | [.labels.comparison_side[0], .labels.source_session[0], .value] | @tsv' samples.jsonl | awk -F '\t' '{ops[$1]+=$3; seen[$1 SUBSEP $2]=1} END{for(k in seen){split(k,a,SUBSEP); sess[a[1]]++} for(k in ops) print k, "operations=" ops[k], "sessions=" sess[k]}' | sort
quantitative_evidence.finding: Repeated results totaled 1,485 candidate operations across 88 candidate sessions versus 224 base operations across 20 base sessions: 6.63× as many operations and 4.4× as many affected sessions.

quantitative_evidence.command: jq -r '[.labels.comparison_side[0],.value]|@tsv' samples.jsonl | awk -F '\t' '{v=$2<0?-$2:$2; total[$1]+=v} END{for(k in total)print k,total[k]}' | sort
quantitative_evidence.finding: The package contains 7,366 candidate operations and 3,780 base operations. Thus repeated results comprise 20.16% of candidate operations versus 5.93% of base operations, a 3.40× relative overrepresentation.

quantitative_evidence.command: jq -r 'select(.stack_frames[0]=="result:repeated") | [.stack_frames[2],.value]|@tsv' samples.jsonl | awk -F '\t' '{s[$1]+=$2;p[$1]+=($2>0?$2:0);n[$1]+=($2<0?-$2:0)}END{for(k in s)printf "%d\t%d\t%d\t%s\n",s[k],p[k],n[k],k}' | sort -nr | head -3
quantitative_evidence.finding: The largest repeated-action excesses were click (+639; 679 candidate versus 40 base), no-op (+356; 441 versus 85), and scroll (+277; 278 versus 1), showing that the recurrence spans multiple action types.
